title: What's the best AI Stack to Generate game Assets?
author: Far_Anything_1049
selftext:
Hello guys, 

I am new to game dev.

I wanted to know what AI tools you guys use for content generation and polishment for your games?

Feel free to share any useful links :) 

Thank you

comments.author: No-Trouble-9138
comments.body:
ChatGPT is the best for tilesets, concepts, views.

Meshy is great for high poly, and Tripo for lowpoly/retopology/pbr.

replies.author: Far_Anything_1049
replies.body: Could you briefly explain these 3 terms ?

replies.author: No-Trouble-9138
replies.body: Which terms?

replies.author: Far_Anything_1049
replies.body: Low poly / retropology , and what do you mean by videos in game dev, like when do you use each one of them

replies.author: No-Trouble-9138
replies.body:
So you are making a game. Lowpoly means that the 3D object can be used in games because it doesn't require a powerful graphic card. Retopology is the process of converting highpoly to lowpoly. So you need Tripo.

 You can use free ChatGPT accounts to generate a view of the object you want, without background The use Tripo's image to 3D object. Then generate texture. Then PBR. Download as FBX for Blender and import in your engine.

replies.author: No-Trouble-9138
replies.body: Tripo has a subscription model. Let me know if you need help to set them up.

replies.author: Far_Anything_1049

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: Is Tripo better than Meshy?

replies.author: No-Trouble-9138
replies.body: Meshy is better at highpoly, but Tripo is better at lowpoly. I always convert images in Meshy first, then retopo/pbr in Tripo. Then use a realtime LOD solution to fully optimize them.

comments.author: EpicOfBrave
comments.body:
Blender and Substance Painter for Mobile Games.

We were able to optimize our 3d models 90%. When using plain AI to generate 3d models we always had either wrong topology or wrong animations or bad textures.

replies.author: Far_Anything_1049
replies.body:
Do you generate the content on blender using claude or any image to 3d model? 
I am building the game for pc, do you think the same stack would work for me ?

replies.author: EpicOfBrave
replies.body: I use Character Creator for the base meshes. Then 3d assets from different places across the internet. Then in Blender combine everything and optimize. Then in substance painter paint everything and generate the textures. Our goal is to have a project on which we can further iterate and when we release a new skin for any of the heroes we can quickly do this.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
So the main issue with using a standard AI tool like Nano Banana for spritesheet animations like walking is that those models can't output transparency, and models like GPT image gen and nano banana have no concept of animation frames, movement, and alignment between frames. You'll spend more time cleaning up the output than you saved generating it.

https://i.redd.it/pn5u9osew9ah1.gif

I actually ran into this enough that I ended up building GameLab Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) . It handles transparent spritesheets, consistent angles/palette across frames, and tileable textures.

Thank you! We do specialize in low resolution (pixel art) but also support any art style, whether that’s photorealistic, or cartoon, isometric etc.

I should mention that this is only for 2d assets.
